title: fix: reject ports in iOS gateway host fields
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the iOS manual Gateway forms accepting a hostname with an embedded port in the Host field. For example, `gateway.example.com:8443` bypassed the existing host-only guidance because the shared endpoint builder treated every colon-containing value as IPv6 and bracketed it before constructing the URL.

## User Impact

Users now see the existing “Enter only a host name or IP address.” guidance and cannot start a connection until the port is moved to the separate Port field. Valid DNS names and IPv4 addresses continue to work, as do raw, bracketed, scoped, private, and public IPv6 literals. The change does not alter stored Host values, context paths, port bounds, authentication, TLS, permissions, or local-network policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

`GatewayConnectEndpoint` is the shared URL-construction owner used by both manual iOS forms and setup paths. It now asks the existing `LoopbackHost` normalization and Network `IPv6Address` parser whether a value is actually an IPv6 literal before adding brackets. This keeps the decision in the shared owner, preserves the original Host bytes, and avoids duplicating validation in either UI caller or adding another parser.

The shared security suite adds the missing regression for a hostname carrying a port. Existing controls continue to cover DNS, IPv4, raw and bracketed IPv6, scoped IPv6, public IPv6 setup payloads, and encoded context paths. The existing iOS host-only assertion is unchanged.

## Evidence

- A scheduled xcode-27 lifecycle run exposed the unchanged iOS assertion for `gateway.example.com:8443`; source and history trace the regression to the broad colon-based bracketing introduced for raw IPv6 support.
- On the exact candidate tree, remote `git diff --check` and Swift parsing pass. The commit-time protocol and native localization guards also pass.
- Exact-head `macos-swift (packages)` passed the new embedded-port regression, existing DNS/IPv4/raw/bracketed/scoped IPv6 controls, and the full 2,374-test OpenClawKit run.
- Exact-head `ios-build (tests)` passed under Xcode 27.1 / Swift 6.4. The build ran SwiftFormat and SwiftLint, compiled the unchanged `GatewayConnectionSecurityTests`, and passed the 668-test lifecycle batch containing that suite.
- Independent calibrated review and the separate canonical autoreview found no actionable defect. ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head at Gold overall / Platinum patch quality with no findings; the requested native proof is now complete.
- Ordinary PR CI’s release-screenshot packaging failed only because the hosted runner moved to Xcode 27.1 while that evidence step still expected Xcode 27.0. The capture itself completed, and the maintained exact-head iOS owner above passed on Xcode 27.1; this environment-version mismatch is unrelated to the three Swift files in this PR.

Visual before/after media cannot be produced with the approved tooling: the available native fallback has no iOS simulator runtime, while the maintained release screenshot fixture intentionally hides manual Gateway controls. The exact-head unchanged validator assertion and shared endpoint controls passed as the strongest substitute; no screenshot, recording, or manual UI pass is claimed here.
